question:
A classroom coding model represents an original column matrix $X$ by an encoded matrix $Y=AX$, where $A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 0\\0 & 1 & 1\\1 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$. The encoded data received by a student is $Y=\begin{bmatrix}4\\4\\5\end{bmatrix}$. To recover the original data, the student must calculate the minors and cofactors of $A$, construct its adjoint, and use the inverse matrix. The determinant must first be checked to ensure that decoding is possible.

(a) Evaluate $|A|$ and determine whether $A^{-1}$ exists.

(b) Find the cofactor matrix of $A$.

(c) Obtain $\operatorname{adj}A$ and $A^{-1}$.

(d) Decode the data by calculating $X=A^{-1}Y$.
explanation:
(a)
Expanding along the first row,
$$|A|=1\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1\\0 & 1\end{vmatrix}-2\begin{vmatrix}0 & 1\\1 & 1\end{vmatrix}$$
$$|A|=1-2(-1)=3$$
Since $|A|=3\neq0$, the inverse of $A$ exists.

(b)
Using the minors and the sign pattern of cofactors, the cofactors are
$$A_{11}=1,\quad A_{12}=1,\quad A_{13}=-1$$
$$A_{21}=-2,\quad A_{22}=1,\quad A_{23}=2$$
$$A_{31}=2,\quad A_{32}=-1,\quad A_{33}=1$$
Therefore, the cofactor matrix is
$$C=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & -1\\-2 & 1 & 2\\2 & -1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$

(c)
The adjoint is the transpose of the cofactor matrix:
$$\operatorname{adj}A=C^T=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 2\\1 & 1 & -1\\-1 & 2 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$
Hence,
$$A^{-1}=\frac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj}A$$
$$A^{-1}=\frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 2\\1 & 1 & -1\\-1 & 2 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$

(d)
$$X=A^{-1}Y$$
$$X=\frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 2\\1 & 1 & -1\\-1 & 2 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}4\\4\\5\end{bmatrix}$$
$$X=\frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}4-8+10\\4+4-5\\-4+8+5\end{bmatrix}=\frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}6\\3\\9\end{bmatrix}$$
Therefore,
$$X=\begin{bmatrix}2\\1\\3\end{bmatrix}$$
The decoded data is $2$, $1$, and $3$.

options.C:
(a) $|A|=0$, so $A^{-1}$ does not exist
(b) $C=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&-1\\-2&1&2\\2&-1&1\end{bmatrix}$
(c) $\operatorname{adj}A$ exists but $A^{-1}$ does not
(d) The data cannot be decoded uniquely
